items.title: Kering Sees Signs of Progress in Curbing Sales Declines at Gucci
items.summary: Bloomberg's earnings coverage frames Gucci's narrowed Q2 comparable sales decline (to roughly 2%, from an 8% Q1 drop) as tentative progress rather than a confirmed turnaround, noting analysts still want several more quarters of evidence before calling Gucci's slump over, and that leather goods returning to growth was the most closely watched data point.

items.title: Gucci Isn't Kering's Only Issue
items.summary: BoF briefing widens the lens beyond Gucci's slightly-better quarter to argue Kering's group-wide turnaround is still fragile, pointing to soft performance at Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga and McQueen, and cautioning against reading Gucci's narrower decline as proof the broader group crisis is resolved.

items.title: EU Fines Gucci, Chloe and Loewe EUR157m for Anticompetitive Resale-Pricing Practices
items.summary: Legal/regulatory analysis of the European Commission's fine against Gucci (part of a combined ~EUR157-182m penalty with Chloe and Loewe) for restricting retailers' ability to discount and deviate from recommended resale prices, which the Commission says raised prices and limited consumer choice; kept in the pool as still-cited background regulatory context feeding ongoing European price-hike criticism, flagged here for freshness caution (originally October 2025) but recurring in August coverage of luxury pricing practices.

items.title: Kering's Gucci Shows Early Signs of Improvement, Analysts Maintain Neutral Rating
items.summary: Equity-research note from Jelena Sokolova calls Gucci's Q2 revenue/margin/regional trends 'encouraging' but keeps a neutral long-term rating, explicitly noting the improvement needs several more quarters of confirmation, especially in China, before it can be treated as a real recovery rather than a base-effect bounce.

items.title: Gucci Seemingly on Cusp of Turnaround
items.summary: UK trade press concludes the turnaround 'still seems a tough proposition' despite better Q2 optics: H1 2026 revenue of about EUR2.76bn was down 9% reported / 5% like-for-like, with COO Jean-Marc Duplaix noting Gucci's brand perception is strongest in North America but weaker footfall in Asia-Pacific ex-Japan (still Gucci's largest market at 31% of retail sales) drove a 5% regional revenue fall.

items.title: Kering to Close 100 More Stores Amid Sales Slump, Including Gucci Locations
items.summary: Coverage of Kering's H1 results highlights the group closed 84 net stores in H1 2026 (following 75 in 2025), on track for a 100-store full-year target and a longer-run plan of roughly 250 closures over four years, framed as evidence the 'recovery' narrative still comes with real footprint contraction and lost sales density in the near term, including at Gucci.

items.source: 36Kr (EU edition) / analyst commentary on Gucci desirability
items.title: Why Don't Rich People Buy Gucci Anymore?
items.summary: Analyst-sourced piece argues Gucci's 2022-2025 revenue loss of over EUR4.5bn stems from over-expansion into streetwear and over-distribution ('too many shops'), which analysts say eroded exclusivity and desirability among core wealthy clientele; used here as recurring critical framing still being cited in early-August turnaround commentary despite being a mid-July piece.

items.title: r/handbags thread continues debating Borsetto/Paparazzo pricing vs perceived quality
items.summary: Community discussion running into the first week of August continues to weigh Demna-era Borsetto and Paparazzo bags against older Marmont/Dionysus pricing; several commenters say construction and leather quality have not visibly improved to match retail price levels, while a smaller group says the new styles are 'finally worth carrying again.' Per-post engagement metrics not retrievable via public search; recorded as null.

items.title: PurseForum/PurseBlog Gucci threads split on 'La Famiglia' bag drops
items.summary: Ongoing PurseBlog/PurseForum coverage and linked member threads on Demna's Gucci output remain polarized in early August: some members welcome the return to recognizable Gucci codes (Horsebit, Web stripe) on the new Borsetto, calling the house 'young again,' while others call recent drops 'underwhelming' versus the hype and say they've stopped tracking new releases. Thread-level like/reply counts not retrievable via public search; recorded as null.

items.title: Trustpilot reviews keep flagging repair delays and hardware/leather durability complaints
items.summary: Rolling UK/global Trustpilot review signal continues to surface recurring complaints about slow official repair turnaround, hardware tarnishing, and leather cracking shortly after warranty windows close; retained as a standing quality-complaint community channel since brand-keyword news search structurally undersamples this feedback per the anti-bias balance duty.

items.title: Gucci Instagram grid continues Borsetto/La Famiglia push; comments mix praise and price pushback
items.summary: Gucci's official Instagram feed continued posting Borsetto/Paparazzo product imagery and La Famiglia campaign content into the first week of August; visible comment threads show a recurring split between styling praise and price-complaint replies, some still referencing the earlier February AI-image backlash from Demna's debut season even though current posts are photographer-shot. Individual post like/comment counts not exposed via public search; recorded as null per policy.

items.title: Kering Shares Surge 15% on Gucci's Promising Turnaround Momentum
items.summary: WWD reports Kering shares closed up nearly 17% at EUR292.85 after Q2 results, crediting Demna's new Borsetto and Paparazzo bag launches and stronger US demand; HSBC upgraded Kering to 'buy' with a raised target, while cautioning the firm does not expect Gucci to return to positive growth this year despite the improved trajectory.
